intents.statement: Everything recorded in Athena should be attributable to a project, a version and an environment.
A team should be able to see which commit a recorded result came from.
A team should be able to see whether a version was buildable and where it is running.
A team should be able to tell when a service's published contract no longer matches the service.
A team should be able to record what was tested against a version and what the outcome was.
A team should be able to compare performance between two versions of the same service.
Every recorded action should name the user it is attributed to.

specifications.statement: When a project is created with a code that is already in use, the request is rejected with 409 and no project is created.
When a project id that does not exist is requested, the response is 204 with no body, not 200 with an empty object.
An environment always belongs to exactly one project, and creating one against an unknown project id is rejected.
A version name is unique within its project, so two versions of one project cannot share a name.
Every write records the user that made it, and a write with no resolvable user is rejected rather than recorded as anonymous.
Registering a repository that is already registered returns the existing repository rather than creating a second one.
A commit sha is recorded once; re-posting the same sha for the same repository does not change the stored record.
A commit trend covers a requested date range, and a range with no commits returns 204 rather than an empty 200.
A pipeline is scoped to one project and one environment, and both must exist before it can be created.
A pipeline execution ends in exactly one of running, passed, failed or aborted, and a status outside that set is rejected.
Pod records are read from the cluster and are never created by a client, so a client POST to the pod collection is rejected.
A drift report names each endpoint that the published spec declares and the running service does not answer, and each the service answers and the spec omits.
A spec freshness response states when the document was last read from the service, and a spec never read reports no timestamp rather than the epoch.
A test item keeps its identity when its title is edited, so past executions stay attached to it.
A test item references a priority and a status that already exist, and a reference to an unknown one is rejected with 400.
A test cycle names exactly one version, and every execution inside it is attributed to that version.
A test execution records one of passed, failed, blocked or skipped, and re-running an item adds an execution rather than overwriting the previous one.
A metric is stored with both a version and an environment, and a metric missing either is rejected at write time.
A metric trend compares only metrics that share a name, a project and an environment, so two environments are never averaged together.
